definitions.explanation: A plant (Persicaria tinctoria) from which indigo dye is extracted. Cultivated in Japan for centuries for textile dyeing.
The deep blue color or dye produced from the indigo plant. One of the most important traditional dye colors in Japan.

notes:
One of the most culturally significant colors in Japan. The indigo plant ({蓼藍|たであい}) has been cultivated in Japan for over a thousand years, and indigo dyeing (⟦{藍染|あいぞ}め→藍染め：23047_aizome⟧) remains an important traditional craft.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{藍染|あいぞ}め→藍染め：23047_aizome⟧: indigo dyeing
- ⟦{藍色|あいいろ}→藍色：15519_aiiro⟧: indigo color
- {藍|あい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{建|た}てる→建てる：01189_tateru⟧: to prepare an indigo dye vat (technical term)
- {藍|あい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{葉|は}→葉：02241_ha⟧: indigo leaves

PROVERB:
⟦{青|あお}→青：02841_ao⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{藍|あい}⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧{出|い}でて{藍|あい}⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦{青|あお}し→青い：00586_aoi⟧ — "Blue comes from indigo yet is bluer than indigo." Meaning: the student surpasses the master. One of the most well-known Japanese proverbs.

CULTURAL NOTE:
{徳島県|とくしまけん} (Tokushima Prefecture) has been the center of indigo production in Japan since the Edo period. The deep blue of indigo-dyed textiles was so characteristic of Japan that visiting Westerners in the Meiji era coined the term "Japan Blue." Today, ⟦{藍染|あいぞ}め→藍染め：23047_aizome⟧ workshops are popular tourist experiences.
